question: Can māyā arise for one established in pure opening?
premises: For one established only in the opening of consciousness, māyā is rootless.
In the method of the unsurpassed self, much explanation is unnecessary.
inference: In the unsurpassed self, māyā cannot arise for one abiding in pure opening.
plain_english: For one who rests only in the opening of consciousness, that māyā is rootless and cannot arise; so what is the use of saying more in this method of the unsurpassed self?
